# GIT012: AI attribution in commit message or PR description

## Error

A commit message or a pull request description contains AI-generated attribution (e.g.,
"Generated by Claude", "Generated with GitHub Copilot", or
"Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex").

A line counts as attribution when it names an AI assistant (Claude, Copilot, Codex) next to a credit marker - "generated", "made with", "co-authored by", the robot emoji - when it carries an assistant session link or the assistant's own address, or when it is nothing but a link to an assistant, which is the shape of a footer whose wording sits on the line above. Naming an assistant without crediting it ("we should try Claude Code for this") is not attribution, and neither is citing vendor documentation in prose. Cyrillic look-alike letters are folded onto their Latin twins, so a homoglyph spelling is read as the name it imitates.

For pull requests every way of writing a description is checked: `gh pr create`, `gh pr edit` and `gh pr merge` (title, inline `--body`/`-b`, heredoc, and the contents of a `--body-file`/`-F` - a squash merge's `--body` becomes the commit body), REST and GraphQL calls that write a pull request (`gh api .../pulls`, `curl` to the same endpoint, `createPullRequest`/`updatePullRequest` mutations, and any `--input`/`--data @file` body they read), and MCP tools such as `create_pull_request`.

For commits the whole command is checked as well, so a second `-m`, a `--trailer`, or a `--message=`/`--file=` spelling cannot carry a footer past the message rules. `git merge`, `git revert`, `git cherry-pick` and `git tag` write a message too and are checked for attribution alone.

Unlike most codes, GIT012 ships with the exception token disabled: an `# EXC:GIT012:...` comment does not downgrade the block, because the assistant writing the commit could just as easily write the token. Set `allow_exception = true` under `[exceptions.policies.GIT012]` to reopen it.

## Why this matters

The commit author takes responsibility for the changes, so commits should be
attributed to the human who reviewed and approved them. AI attribution in git
history can also create legal and compliance complications.

## How to fix

Remove AI attribution from commit messages:

```bash
# Wrong:
git commit -sS -m "feat(api): add endpoint

Generated by Claude"

# Correct:
git commit -sS -m "feat(api): add endpoint"
```

Remove it from PR descriptions the same way:

```bash
# Wrong:
gh pr create --title "feat(api): add endpoint" --body "Summary

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)"

# Correct:
gh pr create --title "feat(api): add endpoint" --body "Summary"
```

## Configuration

Disable this check in `config.toml`:

```toml
[validators.git.commit.message]
block_ai_attribution = false

[validators.git.pr]
block_ai_attribution = false
```

## Hook output

When this error is triggered, klaudiush writes JSON to stdout:

**permissionDecisionReason** (shown to Claude):

- `[GIT012] Commit message contains AI attribution. Remove AI attribution from the commit message or PR description`
- `[GIT012] PR contains AI attribution - remove any AI generation attribution. Remove AI attribution from the commit message or PR description`

**systemMessage** (shown to user):
Formatted error with fix hint and reference URL.

**additionalContext** (behavioral guidance):
`Automated klaudiush validation check. Fix the reported errors and retry the same command.`
